Empirical Research Plan – 19th-Birthday Loss of Coverage and Hospital Use

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Strategy: Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (RDD) with an IV interpretation (“RD-IV”).

Why it fits:
•  Insurance loss is an abrupt contractual rule that takes effect in the **month a person turns 19**.  
•  The running (forcing) variable—age measured in months or days—is continuous and cannot be precisely manipulated by agents.  
•  Crossing the cutoff does not deterministically remove coverage, but it reduces coverage by 5-8 p.p.; hence a **fuzzy** design.  
•  Using the 19-indicator as an instrument for actual coverage lets us estimate the Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) of insurance on hospital utilization.

We will complement the RDD with event-study graphs (RDD-style bins) and subgroup analyses by hospital ownership.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable
•  INSURED_i = 1 if individual i reports any private or Medicaid coverage; 0 if uninsured.

Instrument / discontinuity
•  POST19_i = 1 if age_in_months ≥ 0 (i.e., the first day of the 19th-birthday month or later); 0 otherwise.

Control group
•  Individuals just **below** the 19 cutoff (e.g. 18 y 10 m–18 y 11 m). Their potential outcomes represent the counterfactual utilization absent the insurance loss.

Running variable and cutoff
•  running_i = age in months minus 228 (19 × 12).  
•  Cutoff c = 0.

Treatment timing
•  Event date = first day of the month in which the 19th birthday occurs (data are monthly).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff  
   – Other determinants of ED/inpatient use vary smoothly with age; nothing else jumps exactly at 19.  
   – Plausible: legal majority is 18, alcohol 21; no national policy kicks in at 19.

A2. No precise manipulation of age  
   – Birth dates are exogenous; cannot be timed to avoid insurance loss. Plausible.

A3. First-stage relevance  
   – Private coverage falls 5-8 p.p. at 19 (documented in NHIS). Strong, verifiable.

A4. Stable composition around the cutoff  
   – Population density by single-month age should be smooth; will test with McCrary density test.

A5. Local LATE generalises to near-19 population  
   – We only claim effects for compliers within a few months of 19; policy-relevant for young adults.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Simultaneous school graduation effects  
   – High-school completion also happens near 18–19 and could alter utilisation.  
   Remedy: control flexibly for current school enrolment (NHIS) or restrict to non-students.

T2. Pregnancy-related Medicaid eligibility (discontinuous at 19 for women)  
   – Could confound utilisation changes for female visits.  
   Remedy: run separate RD for males; include interaction POST19×Female.

T3. Coding of age in hospital data (heaping at whole years)  
   – Utilisation files list age in years + months; if some states round months, discontinuity could blur.  
   Remedy: perform state-by-state RD; use only states with true month granularity; show robustness to alternative bandwidths.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
#------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
#------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)       # OLS & IV with fixed effects
library(rdrobust)     # non-parametric RD
library(ggplot2)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data (assume csvs in working directory)
#------------------------------------------------------------
nhis  <- fread("nhis_1997_2007_18to20.csv")
ed    <- fread("ed_visits_5states_04_07.csv")
adm   <- fread("inpatient_6states.csv")
pop   <- fread("census_pop_single_month_age.csv")  # denominator for rates

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Construct running var and treatment
#------------------------------------------------------------
for(dt in list(nhis, ed, adm)) {
  dt[, age_months := age_years*12 + age_month]            # supplied variables
  dt[, run     := age_months - 19*12]                     # centred at 0 = 19th bday month
  dt[, post19  := as.integer(run >= 0)]
}

# Insurance variable (NHIS only)
nhis[, insured := as.integer(private==1 | medicaid==1)]

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. First-stage & reduced-form (NHIS, individual-level)
#------------------------------------------------------------
# Local linear ±12-month bandwidth
bw <- 12
nhis_loc <- nhis[abs(run) <= bw]

# First stage
fs <- feols(insured ~ post19 + run, data = nhis_loc)
summary(fs)

# Reduced form: probability of ED use last year (example outcome)
rf <- feols(ed_any ~ post19 + run | 0, data = nhis_loc)
summary(rf)

# 2SLS: effect of insurance on ED use
iv <- feols(ed_any ~ 1 | insured ~ post19 + run, data = nhis_loc)
summary(iv)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Hospital files – construct rates by age-month-state
#------------------------------------------------------------
# ED example
ed[, cell_id := .(state, year, month, age_months)]
ed_agg  <- ed[, .N, by = .(state, year, month, age_months, run, post19, hosp_owner)]
pop_agg <- pop[, .(population = sum(pop)), 
               by = .(state, year, month, age_months)]
ed_agg  <- merge(ed_agg, pop_agg, by = c("state","year","month","age_months"))

ed_agg[, rate := 1e3 * N / population]     # visits per 1,000

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. RD-IV on rates (state FE, hosp-owner heterogeneity)
#------------------------------------------------------------
ed_bw <- ed_agg[abs(run)<=12]

iv_ed <- feols(rate ~ 1 | insured_share ~ post19 + run | state + hosp_owner,
               data = ed_bw)       # insured_share from NHIS matched at state*year
summary(iv_ed)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Non-parametric rdrobust check (reduced form)
#------------------------------------------------------------
rdrobust(y = ed_agg$rate, x = ed_agg$run, c = 0, p = 1)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Placebo at age 20
#------------------------------------------------------------
ed_agg[, run20 := age_months - 20*12]
ed20 <- ed_agg[abs(run20)<=12]
feols(rate ~ I(run20>=0) + run20, data = ed20)  # expect ≈0
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic priors: Losing coverage raises the out-of-pocket price for non-urgent outpatient care, possibly shifting some cases toward the ED (safety-net) and discouraging inpatient admissions that can be postponed.

Direction:  
•  Probability insured –5 to 8 p.p. at 19 (first stage).  
•  ED visit rate: expected **increase** of ~5–10 % (≈2–3 visits per 1,000 young adults per year).  
•  Inpatient admissions: **decrease** or no change (magnitude –1 % to –3 %).  
•  Larger ED increase at public hospitals (better at treating uninsured).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1. No sorting/manipulation of running variable  ………………… 1  
C2. Smooth baseline covariates at cutoff  …………………………… 1  
C3. No other policy/behavioral jump at 19  ………………………… 0.8 (small concern about school exit)  
C4. Strong first stage (coverage drop)  …………………………… 1  
C5. Robust to bandwidth & functional-form choices  …………… 0.8  

Overall ≈ 4.6 / 5.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
